newsitem.title: USA: Geneva to market anti-ulcer product Aug.30.
newsitem.headline: Geneva to market anti-ulcer product Aug.30.

text.p: Novartis AG's Geneva Pharmaceuticals Inc said Friday a summary judgment was issued in its favor in a patent infringement suit against Glaxo Wellcome Plc regarding the generic equivalent of the anti-ulcer medication Zantac.
Geneva said it will begin supplying the product, called ranitidine hydrochloride, to customers on August 30.
Glaxo Wellcome was not immediately available to comment.
Geneva said the suit, brought by Glaxo Wellcome, was concluded when a U.S. District Court issued a summary judgment in its favor.
Geneva said the litigation would not have prevented it from marketing ranitidine on August 30.
Geneva also said it has received the first tentative approval for ranitidine capsules.
Geneva said Glaxo has claimed the capsules infringe upon its patent.
The capsule version of Zantac has annual U.S. sales of about $300 million.

"We don't think this will substantially change the situation with generic ranitidine as it stands now," said Ramona Jones, a Glaxo Wellcome spokeswoman. "There is currently a generic ranitidine on the market."
